# Field

A label, control, hint and error laid out together, the same way every time.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Dense data</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-field--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:light" title="Field examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-field--docs">Open Field in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-field--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Dense data:** Lays out label, control and error the same way everywhere.

- **Use it when:** Every form control that needs a label, a hint or an error.
- **Not when:** A control that is not part of a form, such as a search box in a toolbar.

Instead:

- [Label](./label.md): The label on its own.

## How Dense data uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Field label or column header</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> type.label</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> type.heading</div></div><div class="cap">Headers repeat on every column; a heavy style would compete with the data.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">An error message</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> color.status.danger with an icon</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> color.status.warning</div></div><div class="cap">Red always means fix this, and the icon says it without color.</div></div></div>

## Why it works this way

Field looks the way it does because of 4 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Field, and what would move if it changed.

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] The label, hint and error are linked to the control, so they are read with it. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add field
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Field reads 30 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Field's tokens to change Field alone.
